claims.text: Coupled tribo-corrosion degradation in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by mechanically induced dynamic refinement of the surface microstructure.
High-strain-rate sliding induces near-surface grain refinement and possibly amorphization in the HEA.
An ultrafine or nanocrystalline HEA microstructure can soften through inverse Hall-Petch behavior.
Dynamic refinement lowers the surface shear strength.
Lower surface shear strength from refinement improves wear resistance.
Grain boundaries in the refined surface act as sites for passive-film formation.
The increased grain-boundary density makes the passive film more defective or less robust and thereby increases localized corrosion.
The corrosion resistance of a Cantor-type HEA can vary with processing-induced microstructure and residual stress.
Cold rolling introduces deformation, while subsequent heat treatment promotes recrystallization in Cantor-type HEAs.
Heat treatment restores a coarse, uniform microstructure and minimizes residual stress relative to the cold-rolled condition.
A Cantor-type HEA initially has a stable passive film in non-aggressive environments.
Relative to the heat-treated coarse-grained baseline, the dynamically refined HEA will have a lower wear rate during tribo-corrosion.
Relative to the heat-treated coarse-grained baseline, the dynamically refined HEA will have a higher corrosion rate during tribo-corrosion.
Total degradation is governed by the balance between improved wear response and deteriorated corrosion protection.
The proposed coupling should dominate only when loading is sufficient to produce pronounced surface refinement.
Removing chemically reactive species can suppress oxide-film effects on deformation and wear and therefore shift the coupled response.
Microalloying that reinforces passive-film stability can cause the proposed refinement-mediated coupling to cease dominating.
The wear-corrosion trade-off varies with alloy composition, passive-film chemistry, and the extent of mechanical deformation.
The threshold strain rate required to trigger surface refinement varies among HEAs.
